canon_read.use: §3.4.3 "QA evidence is persisted in the repository. It is never left only in temporary or scratch storage." (PART-12, used verbatim). §3.4.14 Evidence binding and Step discipline, §3.3 environment-blocked requirements called out and deferred (PART-11 coherence tests, QA-50 re-runs). §3.6 "update the affected QA Plan through its actual review owner" and §10.6 step 5 "Later QA retains Kronos's evidence/Plan responsibilities": the actors DN-5 (a) routes (Kronos revises at QA-80, Isis reviews at QA-70). §3.5.7 read: its "present but not indexed" rule is vendor-step scoped (L-B11), no op.

canon_read.title: PF27-Canon-Plan-Templates
canon_read.sections: Live QA Plan approval materiality discipline (in full); also read in full: Evidence coverage and optional legacy-token binding; Redline bundle construction discipline; Review stability and no-moving-target discipline; Plan command, syntax, and example-literalness approval rule; Explicit non-blockers
canon_read.use: Materiality: "clear enough for the assigned operator to execute the QA run and produce a meaningful governed verdict" (coherence test 4, verbatim). Evidence coverage: mechanical PASS/FAIL predicate per check, no check "for good measure" (tests 1 and 3; QA-80 reshape; QA-50). Gate freeze lifted by current-revision text (request 2). One-pass apply simulation (IA-40 applies none of a set with an unapplicable item); request 4 is not built on it (CD-6 condition).

ops.start: Ambiguous, contradictory, or unsupported redlines return to the same Isis reviewer without inference.
ops.new: Ambiguous, contradictory, or unsupported redlines return to the same Isis reviewer at IA-30 as REDLINE_INCOMPLETE, without inference.
ops.why: CD-5: an unapplicable redline continues to IA-30, its reviewer, instead of ending terminally. Names the receiving prompt and state; keeps 'without inference'.

ops.start: Preserve the evidence and return terminally to the exact origin owner identified by the source package.
ops.new: Preserve the evidence and return terminally to the exact origin owner identified by the source package. In either mode, if any redline item is ambiguous, contradictory, unsupported or has an unresolvable target, apply none of the set, advance no Plan or delta version, and return REDLINE_INCOMPLETE as routed below.
ops.why: CD-5: Execute had no step for an unapplicable redline; a redline bundle is applied once as a set (PF27 Redline bundle construction discipline, one-pass apply), so none is applied and no version advances. Insertion after the wrong-lane sentence, which is kept.

ops.start: REDLINE_INCOMPLETE, WRONG_NATIVE_LANE, source/authority failure, or unresolved target identity: terminal return to the same Isis reviewer or actual origin owner with the preserved checkpoint; no continuation block.
ops.new: REDLINE_INCOMPLETE: write a report, at a path under docs/ephemeral/ in the repository, naming each redline item not applied and why, and return it with the redline set and the unchanged pending Plan, approved base or pending delta to IA-30, in the review mode that issued the redlines, same author/reviewer lineage. - WRONG_NATIVE_LANE, source/authority failure, or an unidentified target Plan or delta: terminal return to the same Isis reviewer or actual origin owner with the preserved checkpoint; no continuation block.
ops.why: CD-5 / MB-020: REDLINE_INCOMPLETE leaves the terminal bullet and becomes a nonterminal return to IA-30 (graph: IA-40 -> IA-30 branch). 'unresolved target identity' is narrowed to the target Plan or delta, because an unresolvable redline target is now REDLINE_INCOMPLETE. The bullet's '- ' prefix sits before the span and is kept.

ops.start: Preserve the evidence and return a wrong-lane case to its exact supplied origin owner without executing another workflow.
ops.new: Preserve the evidence and return a wrong-lane case to its exact supplied origin owner without executing another workflow. A redline set that IA-40 returns as REDLINE_INCOMPLETE is received in the review mode that issued it, as an input to that mode; it is not a fourth mode. Require IA-40's report naming each item it could not apply and why, the redline set, the unchanged pending Plan, approved base or pending delta it targeted, and the same IA author/Isis lineage. Decide that mode again on the same artifact: reissue the redlines corrected and complete, each meeting IA-40's exact-redline boundary, or reach another outcome that mode allows.
ops.why: CD-5: IA-30's intake for a returned redline, as an input in its existing three modes (keeps 'These modes never collapse' and the IA-30_REVIEW_MODE vocabulary unchanged). Placed at the end of 'Review modes and inputs', away from W2's business-case sentences in Execute.

ops.section: Execute and decision criteria (new subsection after step 4)
ops.start: Approval is not task selection, execution, PASS, merge, or closure.
ops.new: Approval is not task selection, execution, PASS, merge, or closure. ### Coherence tests Every approval, in either mode, passes and states how it meets each of these tests for the Plan as it will run: - Every listed check runs at least one command whose result decides its status. No placeholder, removed entry or record-only entry is listed as a check. - A requirement blocked by environment, deferred or out of scope is stated in the scope or deferral section, not as a check. - Every check states what it proves that bound CI or PR evidence does not. A criterion that bound evidence already proves is covered by binding that evidence, not by a re-run. No check is included solely for good measure. - The Plan is clear enough for the assigned operator to execute the QA run and produce a meaningful governed verdict. Before issuing a DENY, state the check collection that results once every redline applies, and test it against these coherence tests. A redline set whose result would fail them is rebuilt before it is issued.
ops.why: MB-026 request 1 (PF27 Evidence coverage: every check has a mechanical PASS/FAIL predicate and no check 'for good measure'; PF19 §3.3: environment-blocked requirements are called out and deferred; PF19 §3.4.14 Evidence binding and Step discipline; PF27 Live QA Plan approval materiality: 'clear enough for the assigned operator'). Request 4 is a new QA-70 reviewer duty under Nathan's CD-6 condition, stated as its own duty, not as part of the one-pass apply simulation.

ops.start: Preserve all unaffected Plan content and existing step/attempt/evidence identity.
ops.new: Preserve all unaffected Plan content and the step/attempt/evidence identity of every check that remains.
ops.why: MB-026 cause R3 / request 3: identity is preserved for the checks that remain, not used to keep dropped checks as placeholders.

ops.start: Do not add requirements, silently omit a redline, self-approve, select tasks, execute QA, or declare PASS.
ops.new: Do not add requirements, silently omit a redline, self-approve, select tasks, execute QA, or declare PASS. Then deliver a coherent runbook: a check that no longer runs a command whose result decides its status is dropped from the Plan, not kept as a placeholder or a record-only entry, and its ID is recorded in the redline application report.
ops.why: MB-026 request 3; PF27 Evidence coverage (each check block defines a mechanical PASS/FAIL predicate).

ops.start: cleanup/recovery, and final-report criteria.
ops.new: cleanup/recovery, and final-report criteria. Bind existing CI or PR evidence that already proves a criterion instead of re-running it, and do not duplicate what GitHub or a governed repository artifact already records reliably. A check that re-runs a closed-rails group CI already ran states the gap it closes. No check is included solely for good measure.
ops.why: MB-026 request 5 / cause R5: PF19 §3.4.14 Evidence binding ('Do not duplicate information that GitHub or a governed repository artifact already records reliably'); PF27 Evidence coverage ('MUST NOT include a step or check solely for good measure').
